objectives: Tell from a document whether the person who certified it had the power to do so.
Explain the three ways in which a notary can be substituted.
Say which notarial acts a mayor and a Bulgarian consul may perform.
Explain how a notarial document travels abroad (apostille) and how a foreign translation is used in Bulgaria.

cards.front: Who other than a notary may perform notarial functions?
cards.back: Only persons for whom **a law** provides it ([[znnd:81]]): assistant notaries, substitutes, registration judges, certain municipal officials and consuls.

cards.front: A deed of sale shows "помощник-нотариус" and no "по заместване". What follows?
cards.back: The assistant had no power for a real-estate deed ([[znnd:40:1]]); the act is **null** ([[gpk:576]]). A substitute signs with "по заместване" ([[znnd:46:1]]).

cards.front: How does another notary substitute a colleague?
cards.back: Under a **contract**, only a notary **from the same district**, for up to **two years**; using the archive of the substituted notary but their own signature and seal ([[znnd:47]]).

cards.front: When does the registration judge perform notarial acts?
cards.back: When the district has **no notary**; when nobody substitutes an absent notary (urgent acts); and on documents in the registry archive ([[znnd:48|Art. 48]] and [[znnd:82|82 ЗННД]]).

cards.front: Where may a mayor certify signatures?
cards.back: In a settlement with **no notary and no district court** ([[znnd:83:1]]).
Signatures on unilateral private documents not subject to entry; signature **and** content of a power of attorney under [[zzd:37]]; copies ([[znnd:83:1]]).

cards.front: A mayor certified the signatures on a transfer of OOD shares. What follows?
cards.back: The certification is outside the mayor's powers ([[znnd:83:2]]), and the Commercial Register refuses the entry. Only a notary certifies such signatures ([[tz:129:2]]).

cards.front: In which language must a document be for a Bulgarian consul to certify it?
Who issues the apostille on a Bulgarian notarial certification?
cards.back: The **Ministry of Justice**, within two working days ([[plzp:17а:2|Art. 17а(2)]]–[[plzp:17а:3|(3) ПЛЗП]]).

cards.front: A translator brings a translation of a French deed for use in Bulgaria. What does the office certify?
cards.back: The **translator's signature** on the translation ([[plzp:21а:1]]), not the accuracy of the translation.

cards.front: Where do the fees go when a mayor or a registration judge performs a notarial act?
cards.back: Mayor: to the **municipal** budget; registration judge: to the **state** budget ([[znnd:86]]).

quiz.question: A deed of sale of a house is signed by "помощник-нотариус" without "по заместване". What is your conclusion?
options: The assistant had no power to issue it; the act is null
The act is valid, because the assistant used the notary's seal
The act is valid, if the notary was in the office that day
The act is voidable within three years from its date
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:40:1:1|Art. 40(1) item 1 ЗННД]] excludes real-estate deeds from the powers of an assistant who is not a substitute; an act by a person without the power is null ([[gpk:576]]), whatever seal was used. Only a registered substitute signs such deeds, with "по заместване" ([[znnd:46:1|Art. 46(1)]]).

quiz.question: Notary A from Plovdiv wants Notary B from Sofia to substitute A for two weeks. Is it possible?
options: No; only a notary from the same district may substitute
Yes; a contract between the two notaries filed with the Chamber is enough
Yes; with the consent of the Council of Notaries for the two weeks
Yes; if notary B is also a registered substitute
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:47:1]]: a notary is substituted by another notary from the same district under a contract. Sofia and Plovdiv are different districts, so no contract or consent helps; A can use a substitute assistant ([[znnd:46|Art. 46]]) or inform the registration judge ([[znnd:48|Art. 48]]).

quiz.question: What does a substituting notary from the same district put on the documents?
options: Their own signature and seal, and a note of the substitution
The seal and the signature of the substituted notary
Their own signature under the seal of the substituted notary
The seal of the district court and their own signature
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:47:2]]: the substitute uses the archive of the substituted notary, but puts their own signature and seal and notes the substitution. The seal of the substituted notary stays locked away.

quiz.question: A village has no notary and no district court. A resident needs a power of attorney to sell land. What can the mayor do?
options: Certify the signature and the content of the power of attorney
Issue the notarial deed of sale for the land in the village himself
Certify only the signature; the content needs a notary
Nothing; the resident must travel to a notary in the town
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:83:1]]: in a settlement with no notary and no district court, the mayor certifies the signature and the content of a power of attorney under [[zzd:37]], signatures on unilateral documents not subject to entry, and copies. A deed stays with the notary of the district ([[gpk:570:1]]).

quiz.question: Which certification may a mayor NOT perform?
options: The signatures on a contract for the transfer of shares in an OOD
The signature on a declaration that is not subject to entry in a register
The accuracy of a copy of a diploma for an employer
The signature and the content of a power of attorney for a sale
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:83:2]] excludes the signatures required by [[tz:15:1|Art. 15(1)]], [[tz:129:2|129(2)]] and [[tz:137:6|137(6) ТЗ]]: the transfer of an enterprise, of company shares and the protocols of decisions. The three other acts are in [[znnd:83:1|Art. 83(1)]].

quiz.question: A Bulgarian citizen in Germany needs a power of attorney in Bulgarian to sell a flat in Varna. Where can the signature and content be certified?
options: At the Bulgarian consulate, in Bulgarian
Only at a notary in Varna, where the flat is
At a German notary, without an apostille or a translation
Only at the Ministry of Justice in Sofia
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:84:1]]: a Bulgarian consul certifies the date, the content and the signatures of private documents in Bulgarian that are not subject to entry. A German notary is another way, but the power then needs an apostille and a translation with a certified translator's signature ([[plzp:21а:1]]). A power is not tied to the district of the flat ([[gpk:570:2]]).

quiz.question: A Bulgarian notary certified a signature on a document for use in Italy. Who issues the apostille?
options: The Ministry of Justice
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs
The regional governor
The Notary Chamber
quiz.explanation: [[plzp:17а:2:1|Art. 17а(2) item 1 ПЛЗП]]: for notarial acts and certifications the Ministry of Justice issues the apostille, within two working days ([[plzp:17а:3|Art. 17а(3)]]). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalises documents for countries outside the Hague Convention ([[plzp:6|Art. 6]], [[plzp:7|7]]).

quiz.question: A sworn translator in Sofia translates a Spanish birth certificate for a Bulgarian court. What does a notary certify?
options: The signature of the translator on the translation
The content of the Spanish certificate itself
The accuracy of the translation against the original
Nothing; a sworn translator's stamp is enough
quiz.explanation: [[plzp:21а:1]]: the notary certifies the signature of the translator on a translation made in Bulgaria for use in Bulgaria. The notary does not check the accuracy of the translation or the content of the foreign document.

quiz.question: A district has no notary at all. Who performs notarial acts there?
options: The registration judge at the district court
The mayor of the district centre
The nearest notary of a neighbouring district
The president of the district court of the district
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:82:1]]: in a district with no notary the registration judge performs all notarial acts. A notary of another district may not act outside the district ([[gpk:573:1]]); the mayor acts only where there is also no district court ([[znnd:83:1|Art. 83(1)]]).

quiz.question: How long may a substitution by another notary last?
options: Up to two years from the contract
Up to one month from the contract
Up to six months from the contract
Without a limit, while the contract stands
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:47:4]]: the term of a substitution by another notary may not exceed two years from the conclusion of the contract, the same limit as for a substitute assistant ([[znnd:46:2|Art. 46(2)]]).

quiz.question: A notary falls ill for a week; the office has no substitute. A client needs an urgent certification. What does the law provide?
options: The notary informs the registration judge, who performs the urgent acts
The assistant notary performs all acts until the notary recovers
A notary from the neighbouring district performs the acts in this office
The clerk prepares the acts, and the notary signs them after recovery
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:48:1]]: when the notary is absent and nobody substitutes, the notary informs the registration judge, who takes over the urgent notarial acts. An assistant without entry as a substitute acts only on the notary's instructions ([[znnd:40|Art. 40]]), and no notary acts outside the own district ([[gpk:573:1]]).

quiz.question: A German citizen in Berlin wants the Bulgarian consulate to certify a declaration in Bulgarian for a Bulgarian bank. May the consul do it?
options: Yes; the document is in Bulgarian and takes effect in Bulgaria
No; a consul certifies the documents of Bulgarian citizens only
No; a consul certifies only documents subject to entry
Yes, but only after a translation into German is attached
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:84:1]]: the consul certifies private documents in Bulgarian presented by Bulgarian or foreign citizens; for a foreign citizen [[znnd:84:2|Art. 84(2)]] adds the condition that the document is intended to take effect in Bulgaria. Documents subject to entry are excluded.
